comments.body: Audit started after signed plan PASS and claim. Method defaults adopted from plan-review coaching: use calendar quarters for trends; present every period but mark n<10 as low-sample and avoid directional claims from those periods alone. Validation vocabulary is exactly: VALIDATED = direct evidence supports the bounded claim and no material confounder remains; QUALIFIED = evidence supports a narrower claim, relies on an explicit proxy, or retains a material confounder; REJECTED = evidence does not support the claim or an alternative explanation fully accounts for it. The independent reviewer must return one of these labels with a reason for every draft finding.

comments.body:
## Evidence snapshot and reproducible query logic

Frozen evidence refs: code `11d5994594fce53928a1d6f832b1deaa26e34160` (the `origin/main` tip when commit mining ran); canonical tracker `46168442ee634afe78703ed3f42b9964aba7fa75`. Window: code 2026-06-08 through 2026-08-15 (68.0 days); current work-ticket genesis 2026-06-09 through 2026-08-15 (67.4 days).

Query logic: (1) `rebar export --strip-external` supplied the 2,265 reduced current task/story/bug/epic records; (2) `.tickets-tracker/*/*.json*` supplied 62,390 raw events, deduplicated by event UUID and sorted by event timestamp, including retired pre-compaction events; (3) lifecycle edges came from STATUS `current_status -> status`; plan/code/completion outcomes came from schema-tagged REVIEW_RESULT and COMPLETION_VERDICT records; (4) `git log 11d599... --format=...` plus `--numstat` supplied commit bodies, parents, files, and churn; (5) `rebar metrics --since 2026-06-08 --until 2026-08-15 --output json` cross-checked built-in structural/git metrics. The lagging `.tickets-hotpath-authoritative` worktree was explicitly rejected as a source after a provenance check.

Population/flow: 2,265 current work tickets = 713 tasks, 684 stories, 648 bugs, 220 epics; 2,105 closed (92.9%), 25 open, 17 in progress, 97 idea, 20 archived, 1 blocked. Closed lead time create->last close: p50 0.48d, p90 4.64d (n=2,105). Cycle first in_progress->last close: p50 0.06d/1.44h, p90 0.56d (n=1,898). 59 tickets reopened. 680 discovered_from links: 416 discoveries during source execution and 99 after source close; for bugs alone, 262 during and 55 after.

Planning/gates: plan review existed on 1,364 work tickets. First plan verdict PASS 669 / BLOCK 590 / INDETERMINATE 105: 49.0% first-pass; 654 initially non-PASS tickets later reached PASS; attempts p50=2, p90=8. Review-before-claim adoption rose from 136/465 (29.2%) for Q2-created claimed tickets to 1,155/1,452 (79.5%) in Q3. Completion verdicts existed on 998 tickets: first verdict PASS 722 / FAIL 243 / UNKNOWN 19 / ERROR 14 = 72.3% first-pass; 954 eventually passed. Testing-section tickets were 79.8% first-pass at completion (268/336) versus 68.6% without (454/662); declared file-impact tickets were 74.2% versus 67.7% undeclared. These are observational associations, not causal estimates. Plan reviews consumed 116,560 recorded LLM calls across 4,530 result records, or 114.72 calls per accepted completion-PASS record; this is calls, not currency cost.

Code-review funnel: 1,616 synthetic code-review artifacts, 1,284 linked to work tickets, 1,209 unique Gerrit changes with results. First verdict PASS 1,178 / BLOCK 27 / INDETERMINATE 4 = 97.4% first-pass; results contained 45 blocking and 3,345 advisory findings. Among 39 tickets named as `caused_by` sources, 28/29 with linked code review passed first time (96.6%), indistinguishable from other reviewed tickets (96.5%); initial plan PASS was lower for those sources (10/33=30.3% versus 659/1,331=49.5%). Small-N and blame-attribution selection effects apply.

Defect signals: 648 current bugs. Final close classes: 242 preexisting, 42 plan_defect, 40 regression, 37 env_integration, 17 flaky, 39 duplicate, 22 not_a_bug, 2 undetermined, 207 legacy missing. All 648 current bugs lack a `detected_by:*` tag, so a true bug-escape rate or detection-stage efficiency cannot be calculated. 49 advisory caused_by links cover 39 source tickets; 43 linked bugs were created after the source closed, with lag p50 0.68d/p90 15.14d. This is a proxy: auto-attribution uses majority git blame over recorded impacted files, and the top 8-bug fan-in source is visibly semantically mixed, demonstrating false-positive risk. Caused-by-linked source tickets were much larger than other ticket-linked changes (median total churn 912 vs 256 lines; p90 2,141 vs 847; median source churn 114 vs 34.5), but size also makes blame attribution more likely.

Commit process: 2,349 reachable commits at the frozen code ref; 2,228 non-merges, 121 merges, 2,005 first-parent. First-parent non-merge cadence covered all 68 days: p50 23 commits/active day, p50 inter-commit 16.3 minutes. Q2->Q3 governance adoption: ticket trailer 0%->90.4%, DCO 0%->82.9%, Change-Id 0%->99.3%; all three reached ~100% in the latest full weeks. Across all history 1,394 non-merge commits touched `src/`; 1,221 (87.6%) also touched tests, and current Python test LOC is 2.09x source LOC. Q2->Q3 source-change shape improved: median source churn 111.5->95 lines and share above 400 source lines 20.2%->11.0%, while median test churn on source changes rose 84.5->160.5 lines. Q3 total-change p90 remained ~780 lines. Same-file retouch within 24h was 47.7% of consecutive file-touch pairs; treat this as hotspot/coordination evidence, not proven rework.

Code-health cross-check: built-in metrics report 0 modules over the 800-LOC cap, but 35/495 source modules are near cap; local count shows several at 790-800 LOC, including inbound_differ.py (800), binding_store.py/apply_inbound_records.py (799), signing.py (798), and llm/runner.py (797). Duplication is 4.09% (1,826 clones), and the history shows 820,742 insertions / 189,894 deletions with a 0.231 refactor-to-addition ratio. 115 title/tag debt proxies were found and 112 are closed, showing active debt repayment; the near-cap cluster and high-churn hotspots remain forward risk.

Data limits: only 68 days and two calendar quarters; Q3 is partial. Tracker policy/gates were introduced during the window, so before/after comparisons combine process maturation with workload changes. Ticket classifications and relations are author/bot supplied; missing detected_by data prevents true escaped-defect denominators. Commit author concentration and automated identities make commit count a throughput signal, not person-hours. No production incident/SLO data was available.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Project maintainers need an evidence-backed retrospective of the complete available rebar ticket and Git histories to understand how work actually flows and where process changes could improve quality, reduce escaped defects, move uncertainty into planning, align with rigorous OSS practice, and control code debt. Ticket events and repository commits are the primary evidence; bug tags, reopen/discovery links, and test/fix commits will be treated as imperfect proxies rather than ground truth for production escapes.

## Approach
Perform a read-only mixed-method audit. Extract reproducible aggregate measures over the full available history through 2026-08-15, segment trends by calendar period where sample sizes permit, and inspect representative/outlier tickets and commits to explain the aggregates. Measure ticket mix, lifecycle/throughput, planning and completion-gate signals, dependencies/discovery/rework proxies, commit cadence and size, ticket-trailer/DCO discipline, and code/test/docs change patterns. Keep observation, inference, and limitation separate. Give the resulting evidence table and draft findings to an independent subagent for adversarial validation; retain only findings supported by the evidence and label disputed or proxy-based conclusions. This approach fits because longitudinal counts reveal recurring behavior while sampled records and independent review guard against over-interpreting tracker metadata.

## Scope
- No repository files will be modified.
- Read-only evidence: rebar ticket/event history, relationships and comments exposed by the checkout, plus Git commit and diff metadata reachable from the current repository.
- Durable output: methodology, progress, evidence, findings, limitations, and recommendations will be recorded as comments on this ticket; the synthesized report will also be returned to the requester.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The analysis states the observed time windows, populations, denominators, commands or query logic, and important data-quality limitations; verified by an evidence comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The report quantifies defensible trends in ticket mix and flow, planning/review/completion signals, dependency or rework proxies, commit cadence and sizing, ticket/DCO linkage, and code-versus-test/docs changes; verified against extracted aggregates and representative samples recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] An independent subagent critically checks the evidence-to-claim links, identifies confounders or unsupported conclusions, and the final report labels each material finding as validated, qualified, or rejected; verified by a validation comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The final recommendations are prioritized and tie each proposed process change to a validated finding, a concrete practice, and a measurable leading or lagging indicator for quality, bug escape, planning risk, OSS rigor, or debt; verified by the final ticket comment and requester report.
